title: Ring the Tens

serves.summary: The learner rings groups of ten in a collection of up to 120 objects and types how many, which shows they can count a large collection by making tens.

request.topic: Counting a collection to 120 by making tens
request.objective: Count a collection of up to 120 objects by making groups of ten and write the numeral for how many.

problems.ask: Count the dots. Make groups of ten by dragging through them, then type how many dots there are.
problems.goal: Four groups of exactly ten, 2 dots left loose, and 42 typed. Rows are ten wide and each group shows its count.

problems.ask: Count the stars. Make groups of ten by dragging through them, then type how many stars there are.
problems.goal: Three groups of exactly ten, 7 left loose, and 37 typed. Rows are six wide, so a group runs on to the next row.

problems.ask: Count the squares. Make groups of ten by dragging through them, then type how many squares there are.
problems.goal: Ten groups of exactly ten, 4 left loose, and 104 typed. Ten tens is written as one hundred, not as 10 beside the ones. Group counts are no longer shown.

problems.ask: Count the dots. Some spots are empty. Make groups of ten by dragging through them, then type how many dots there are.
problems.goal: Five groups of exactly ten, 6 left loose, and 56 typed. Each row holds seven, so a row is not a ten.
